observations.code_quote: 2. **Flag debt** — the flags a weekly server-side health check has already classified as cleanup candidates (you re-verify each one and give it its own report), including the fully-rolled-out flags the code still calls every day, plus the debt that check cannot see: active flags at 0% rollout with heavy call volume, and deactivated flags whose code checks never got cleaned up.
observations.posthog_connection: Clarifies the definition of 'Flag debt' in the Signals Scout documentation, potentially aiding team understanding of the cleanup scope.

observations.code_quote: **Rank before you verify.** A roster can carry dozens of stale flags, and re-verification costs several tool calls each against a hard 15-minute run wall — overrun kills the run and loses your anomaly findings with it. Every ranking input arrives in the list response, so ordering the paged set is free. **Drop the flags a live cleanup report already covers before you apply the cap** — the `report:feature-flags:stale:<key>` pointers from the orientation scratchpad search name them for free, and finding them at re-verification instead has already spent the slot. Authoring a report never resolves the health issue; only the check ceasing to emit the flag does, and removing its code checks drives the calls down further, so a reported flag stays active and holds the top of the ranking for good. **Order within an `evidence_class`, never across them** — a day count drawn from a different source is not a stronger case, and one merged list hands every slot to whichever class carries the oldest dates. Inside a class, a large `days_since_evidence` and a deterministic `fully_rolled_out` / `not_rolled_out` direction rank first. Carry at most ~3 into re-verification in total and at most 2 from any one class, so no class takes every slot; fill any remaining slot with the strongest candidate left in any class, and leave it unspent rather than carrying a weak one. Leave the rest ranked in `pattern:feature-flags:stale-queue` for the next run. Rewrite that queue without the flags you reported or dropped as covered, so it drains rather than grows. Say in the close-out how many you deferred; never silently truncate. Forty stale flags is not forty reports today, and it is not forty re-verifications either.

observations.behavior: Documentation update: P1.F2.H3 adds a warning not to archive flags while PostHog is still receiving calls; P1.F2.H4 updates a scratchpad entry example and removes a legacy key.
observations.code_quote: **A stale flag with no code left to remove is not a code change.** `fully_rolled_out_without_usage_data` means no call was ever recorded, which is also the shape of a flag created in the UI and never wired. A completed migration reaches this lane the same way: its checks were removed when the migration finished. Autostarting either opens a draft PR the implementation agent cannot fill, burning a task run and an inbox slot. When the call-site search comes back empty, the remaining work is archival, which this lane never does on its own — file `requires_human_input` saying the flag looks unreferenced and a human should confirm and archive it, or keep it in memory if that decision is not worth an inbox slot. **Never take this route where PostHog is still receiving calls.** On `effectively_full_rollout` a call arrived inside the last 30 days, so an empty call-site search means you searched the wrong repository. Try one more repository, then drop the candidate.
observations.posthog_connection: Clarifies archival behavior for the signals-scout agent, potentially reducing false-positive archival or unnecessary repository searches, but this is a documentation-only change and does not demonstrate implementation or validation.
